unit.why: A continuous narrative about the Saba of Shpola (R. Leib) in exile with R. Mordechai of Neshchiz and the Shatz of Zaslav: the circumcision-feast episode, their escape, and the later visit to Neshchiz and the Saba's revelation.
unit.boundary_note: opens with 'ויהי אחרי הדברים האלה', referring back to earlier tales of the Saba (previous division text not shown); the narrative stands on its own

stories.start_quote: ויהי אחרי הדברים האלה נתוועד הסבא הזה
stories.end_quote: והיו נוסעים אליו מכל המקו מות:
stories.summary_en: While wandering in self-imposed exile, the Saba of Shpola, R. Mordechai of Neshchiz and the Shatz of Zaslav are seated with the poor at a circumcision feast in Vladimir. The two others proclaim each other rabbi of Neshchiz and Shatz of Zaslav, and the angry host strikes R. Mordechai. The Saba hits the host and they all flee, hiding under a bed where they are miraculously not found. R. Mordechai soon becomes a famous rabbi. When the Saba, dressed as a poor man, forces his way in to see him, they quarrel privately. The Saba then serves as a beadle in Zlatopol until he is revealed as a holy man and settles in Shpola.
